inputs.name: semaphore_version
inputs.description: Tag of the docker.io/semaphoreui/semaphore image, such as "v2.19.17". Change image_digest with it.

inputs.name: image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of docker.io/semaphoreui/semaphore for semaphore_version. Podman pulls by the digest, so a tag that moves upstream can't change what runs.

inputs.name: admin
inputs.description: The admin Semaphore creates on its first start, such as { email = "you@example.com" }. Later changes don't touch the account; change it in Semaphore.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password the admin is created with on the first start. It reaches the host in a root-only env file and never the plan or state.

inputs.name: public_url
inputs.description: The address people reach Semaphore at, such as "https://semaphore.example.com". Semaphore uses it in the links it sends, in alerts and in its OIDC callbacks. Sets SEMAPHORE_WEB_ROOT.

inputs.name: postgres
inputs.description: PostgreSQL to keep Semaphore's data in, such as {} for one on the same host. The role and database must exist. When null, Semaphore uses SQLite in /var/lib/semaphore/data. Semaphore picks its database on its first start only.

inputs.name: postgres_password
inputs.description: Password of the postgres username. Needed with postgres. It reaches the host in a root-only env file and never the plan or state.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address Semaphore listens on. The default keeps it on the host, for a reverse proxy with TLS in front.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: More of Semaphore's environment variables, such as { SEMAPHORE_EMAIL_ALERT = "true", SEMAPHORE_EMAIL_PASSWORD = "..." }. They go in a root-only env file and never reach the plan or state.
